findings.surface: moving-target lens set and citation-matcher limits
findings.claim: The "no other lens covers" answer is a time-stamped upper bound, not a stable fact. The first listing of findings/ had 7 files; linkedin-5.json appeared at 19:37; pagination-validation.json was rewritten (38,143 -> 33,916 bytes) and stubs.json (112,810 -> 35,587 bytes) while this audit ran; re-running the identical citation scan moved the cited-row total from 500 to 490 and zero-cited open families from 294 to 296. The matcher counts an open doc only when its exact basename (or full path) appears, a GH issue only via gh#N/GH #N/GitHub issue #N/issue #N/#N, and a stub only via its path/basename; truncated citations ("20261023T124140Z-...") and prose-only references are missed, while bare #N can match line numbers. Thus 490/13041 cited is a LOWER bound on citations and the zero-cited family lists are UPPER bounds.
findings.root_cause: Other lens agents write their findings files concurrently and revise them; the completeness lens has no way to freeze or enumerate the final lens roster, and the corpus has no stable claim-citation syntax.
